turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I guess... well, they brought me in because of what's been happening at work. I work at a warehouse, and... I keep doing things that bother people. Like, sometimes I just freeze with my arms up when I'm standing by the forklift. Or I'll start copying the beeping sounds the machines make, and doing the hand signals the drivers use. And when I'm supposed to be moving boxes, I end up putting them in these strange little patterns instead. People yell at me to stop and do it right, but... I just keep doing it. So they wanted me to come see you.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes freezing in postures, copying sounds and movements (echolalia and echopraxia), and arranging boxes in strange patterns despite being told to stop, which are clear signs of disorganized or abnormal motor behavior.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
turns.patient_response: No, I... I don't think so. I hear the actual machines and the people talking, but... nothing that isn't really there. Nobody's talking to me when I'm alone or anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or sounds that are not really there, stating nobody talks to them when they are alone.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any problems with your memory or your ability to think clearly lately?
turns.patient_response:
I think... yeah, my thinking gets pretty messed up. It's hard to keep my thoughts straight when I talk. Like, when the supervisor asks me which pallets are going on the truck, I'll start trying to explain it to him. But my words just jump around. I'll start talking about the load sheet, and then somehow I'm talking about my old house, and then fishing... and then church boxes. 

I don't really know how I get from one thing to the next, but by the time I'm done talking, nobody knows what I meant. So, yeah, I guess I can't think clearly enough to just answer a simple question anymore.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient describes their speech jumping between unrelated topics (load sheet, old house, fishing, church boxes) to the point that others cannot understand them, indicating derailment and disorganized speech.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient explicitly states that their thinking gets messed up and they cannot think clearly enough to answer simple questions.

Sorry, I... my head is just really mixed up today. No, it is actually happening. I guess that's the main reason they brought me in here.

symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient states their head is mixed up, they get confused, and they lose track of what they are saying, indicating clouded thinking and reduced concentration.
